title: Heat Recovery System
model_title: Run-Around Coil Heat Recovery System (Exhaust → Supply Air)

introduction.definition: A run-around coil heat recovery system recovers heat from exhaust air to preheat the incoming supply air. A finned coil in the exhaust duct heats a pumped water–glycol loop, which carries the heat to a second coil in the supply duct. The two airstreams never meet.
applications: Hospitals, laboratories and clean rooms (no cross-contamination)
Retrofits where ducts are far apart
introduction.summary: A run-around coil heat recovery system recovers heat from building or process exhaust air. A finned coil in the exhaust duct heats a water–glycol loop; a pump carries it to a second coil in the supply duct, which preheats the incoming fresh air. The airstreams never mix.

temperature.description: Warm exhaust air (orange) is cooled by the exhaust coil (blue after the coil), the glycol loop carries that heat to the supply coil, where cold fresh air is warmed. The two airstreams never mix — useful where cross-contamination is not allowed (labs, hospitals). Typical sensible effectiveness is about 45–65 %.

foundation: Mount AHU/coil sections level on a plinth or frame so the drain pan drains fully.
alignment: Seal sections air-tight; install coils in the correct air-flow direction (counter-flow to water).
piping: Pipe with isolation valves, strainer, control valve and balancing valve; trap the condensate drain with a water seal deeper than the fan static pressure.
commissioning: Vent coils, check flow and ΔT, verify valve stroke and control; check that condensate drains; balance air flow.

periodic.task: Check glycol concentration and coil cleanliness.

causes: Very cold supply air, low glycol temperature
Fouled coils, low glycol flow, air in loop

safety: Glycol handling; isolate electrical supply before maintenance.

video_tutorials.title: Heat Recovery System — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Heat Recovery System.
A run-around coil heat recovery system recovers heat from exhaust air to preheat the incoming supply air.
A finned coil in the exhaust duct heats a pumped water–glycol loop, which carries the heat to a second coil in the supply duct.
The two airstreams never meet.
Typical applications include hospitals, laboratories and clean rooms (no cross-contamination); retrofits where ducts are far apart; industrial process exhaust heat recovery.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Circulating Pump (in-line), Exhaust Fan Impeller, Supply Fan Impeller.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: How the Heat Recovery System works.
Warm exhaust air passes the exhaust coil.
The glycol loop absorbs that heat.
The pump circulates glycol to the supply coil.
Cold supply air is warmed by the supply coil.
Fans move both airstreams.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.
Warm exhaust air (orange) is cooled by the exhaust coil (blue after the coil), the glycol loop carries that heat to the supply coil, where cold fresh air is warmed.

video_tutorials.title: Heat Recovery System — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Heat Recovery System.
Check pump and loop temperatures.
Check glycol concentration and coil cleanliness.
Clean coils; replace pump seals.
Watch for frost on exhaust coil: rising ΔP, falling recovery. Common cause: very cold supply air, low glycol temperature.
Watch for low effectiveness: small temperature rise. Common cause: fouled coils, low glycol flow, air in loop.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
